subject: physics

moments.title: Lippershey's spyglass
moments.body: A Dutch spectacle-maker applies for a patent on a tube that makes distant things look near. The application is rejected as too simple to patent. Telescope-makers spring up across Europe.
moments.takeaway: The telescope is invented as a maritime toy.

moments.title: Galileo turns it skyward
moments.body:
Galileo improves the design to 30x magnification and points it at the heavens. In months he sees mountains on the Moon, four moons of Jupiter, phases of Venus, sunspots. He publishes 'Sidereus Nuncius'.

The geocentric universe is empirically wrong.
moments.takeaway: In one winter, Galileo transforms astronomy and threatens the Church's cosmology.

moments.title: Inquisition trials
moments.body: In 1616 the Church bans Copernicanism. Galileo, after publishing 'Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems' in 1632, is tried by the Inquisition, forced to recant, and placed under house arrest for the rest of his life. He continues to work.
moments.takeaway: The Church silences but cannot reverse the scientific revolution.

moments.title: The Vatican apologises
moments.body: The Vatican formally acknowledges Galileo was right. The Church took 359 years to apologise.
moments.takeaway: Institutional admission of error takes centuries.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: The JWST and ELT (39-m European telescope, first light 2028) extend Galileo's work to billions of light years. Adaptive optics correct atmospheric blur. Space-based telescopes resolve features billions of times finer than Galileo's first sketches.
now.open_questions: Can ELT/HabEx directly image Earth-like exoplanets?

reflection: Galileo recanted to save his life but reportedly muttered 'Eppur si muove' — 'and yet it moves'. When should a scientist compromise to survive?
